headline: All majors below the 200-day line with momentum rolling over, but whales buying spot while shorts are getting squeezed at extremes
paragraphs: The regime is clearly bearish on the structure. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, with zero golden crosses to signal a shift. None of them are above the line. Bitcoin sits at 63,054, nearly 50 percent below its 12-month high of 124,740. Ethereum is worse: 61.5 percent down from 4,818. Solana has given up 70.6 percent of its year-high, and Cardano has collapsed 80.5 percent from 0.96. The momentum picture adds to the weakness: RSI-14 readings across the majors are either compressed (Bitcoin at 45.4, Ethereum at 49.8, Solana at 43.2) or sitting neutrally (XRP at 46.5, BNB at 54.0). MACD is beneath the signal line for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and XRP. Only BNB, Doge, and Cardano have MACD above signal, but those three assets are still trapped below their 200-day lines, which means momentum divergence is present: positive MACD cross without a trend recovery. Cardano is the outlier by magnitude, up 8 percent in 24 hours and 12.18 percent over seven days, with RSI at 65.3, but it is the furthest down from its year-high of any major and carries the highest volatility at 65.5 percent over 30 days. Strength in a deeply broken trend is a signal to watch, not to trust.

Derivatives positioning reveals crowding on the long side and funding that is now turning negative, a classic setup for position unwind. Bitcoin open interest stands at 2.01 billion dollars, with a long-to-short ratio of 2.13, meaning roughly two dollars of longs for every short. Ethereum has a 2.17 ratio at 1.33 billion in open interest. Solana is more extreme at 2.92 longs per short, and Doge is deeply crowded at 4.98 longs per short. XRP's ratio sits at 3.22. On the funding side, Bitcoin and Ethereum are both in negative territory: BTC funding is negative 0.0013 percent per 8-hour period (negative 1.4 annualized), ETH at negative 0.0007 percent (negative 0.8 annualized). This means shorts are being paid to hold, a sign that the long premium is being wrung out. Solana flipped positive at 0.0007 percent (0.8 annualized), and XRP is the outlier at positive 0.01 percent per 8-hour (11 annualized), showing longs are still willing to pay. Liquidations over the last 21 to 23 hours have been heavily one-sided: Bitcoin saw 884 total liquidations with 5.26 million in long liquidations versus 3.65 million in shorts. Ethereum's imbalance is starker: 11.48 million in longs liquidated versus 6.71 million in shorts. Solana shows 3.44 million in long liquidations against only 419 thousand in shorts. When one side is getting flushed at eight-to-one ratios, the other side is holding cheap.

Spot flows show a rare alignment: whales are buying into weakness while retail is panicking. Over the last 24 hours, 164.96 million dollars in Bitcoin has moved off exchanges into non-custodial wallets, according to the whale tracker. The source is Crypto.com, a single exchange, so the move is concentrated, but the direction is explicit: a major holder is taking delivery. Ethereum saw a small 9 million inflow over the last five sessions, with same-direction streaks of only two days, so ETH is more contested. Bitcoin spot ETF flows, the traditional finance proxy, are a different message: on July 31st alone, the US Bitcoin ETF saw a 265.4 million dollar net outflow. The last five sessions show a cumulative outflow of 61.5 million, but only one day of same-direction data, meaning the outflows may have come concentrated in a single bad session. The Ethereum ETF is more stable, with 9 million inflow on July 31st and 10 million net positive over five sessions. Stablecoin float sits at 303.81 billion, down 1.59 percent over 30 days, which is a slow bleed of dry powder, not a rout. The weekly whale net flows show violent oscillation: 728 million outflow, then 146 million inflow, then 445 million outflow, then 1.07 billion outflow in the most recent weekly total. The most recent week was the biggest outflow on record in this window, meaning major holders are in withdrawal mode broadly, with today's 164 million move representing a small fraction of that larger trend.

Sentiment is registering fear at 27, sitting near the bottom of its recent 30-day range of 20 to 33. The crowd is nervous, and that matches the tape structurally: all majors below the 200-day, no golden crosses, liquidations running one-sided. But the disconnect lies in the whale move into spot Bitcoin and the negative funding on the major contracts. When shorts are getting paid and whales are taking delivery, the crowd's fear may be pricing in a bounce. The broader market moved 0.06 percent over 24 hours, with Bitcoin dominance holding steady at 56.3 percent, suggesting no rotation toward alts despite the daily movers showing pockets of strength (ADA up 8 percent, BEAT up 21 percent, UB up 17 percent). These are noise in a heavy structure. Bitcoin's 90-day range is 58,566 to 82,018, and price at 63,054 is in the lower half of that band, with only 3 percent upside to the midpoint. Network difficulty is scheduled to retarget in 896 blocks with a 2 percent increase already flagged, which will tighten competition if price does not rise to match.

Watch for three conditions that would signal the picture has shifted. First, a recovery above the 200-day SMA across the majors, especially Bitcoin and Ethereum together. That line is structural and absent a golden cross, the trend remains down by definition. Second, a flip in weekly whale flows to consistent net inflows over two weeks or more. Today's 164 million move off Crypto.com is one event; the 1.07 billion weekly outflow is the story. Third, monitor funding cost direction. If BTC and ETH funding stays negative, shorts are extracting value from longs, which typically precedes a washout of weak long holders. If it flips to positive with the liquidations still running, the long side is being purged and fuel for a move is being loaded. The RSI compression across the board means the market has room to run in either direction, but compression with a below-200-day trend is usually resolved by a deeper retest before any relief.
